items.q: Why is glycine strictly required at every third position (Gly-X-Y repeating sequence) in the primary structure of all fibrillar collagen alpha chains?
o: Glycine has the smallest side chain (single hydrogen) that fits into the restricted central axial core of the triple helix
Glycine is the only amino acid that forms covalent disulfide bridges
Glycine undergoes post-translational hydroxylation to stabilize the helix
Glycine contains a negative charge that repels neighboring tropocollagen fibrils
items.exp: The collagen triple helix is wound so tightly that steric constraints permit only the smallest amino acid, glycine (with a single hydrogen atom side chain), to occupy the inward-facing central axis.
r: Correct. Glycine fits into the crowded central axis of the collagen triple helix.
Incorrect. Cysteine forms disulfide bonds, not glycine.
Incorrect. Proline and lysine are hydroxylated, not glycine.
Incorrect. Glycine is neutral and uncharged.
items.kp: Glycine occurs every third residue in collagen (Gly-X-Y) because its tiny hydrogen side chain is the only residue small enough to fit inside the triple-helix core.

items.q: A sailor on a long voyage develops bleeding spongy gums, perifollicular corkscrew hemorrhages, petechiae, and poor wound healing. What biochemical step in collagen synthesis is impaired by vitamin C deficiency?
o: Hydroxylation of proline and lysine residues in the rough endoplasmic reticulum
Cleavage of terminal propeptides by extracellular peptidases
Deamination of lysine by lysyl oxidase to form allysine crosslinks
Signal peptide cleavage on the nascent pre-procollagen chain
items.exp: Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases require ascorbic acid (vitamin C) as a reducing agent to keep catalytic iron in the ferrous (Fe2+) state. In scurvy, unhydroxylated procollagen fails to form stable triple helices and degrades.
r: Correct. Scurvy impairs vitamin C-dependent prolyl and lysyl hydroxylation.
Incorrect. Propeptide cleavage is extracellular and vitamin C-independent.
Incorrect. Lysyl oxidase requires copper, not vitamin C.
Incorrect. Signal peptidase does not require vitamin C.
items.kp: Scurvy results from vitamin C deficiency, impairing prolyl and lysyl hydroxylation; unstable procollagen degrades, causing capillary fragility and poor wound healing.

items.q: Which extracellular enzyme requires copper as an essential cofactor to deaminate lysine and hydroxylysine residues into allysine aldehydes for covalent collagen crosslinking?
items.exp: Lysyl oxidase is a copper-dependent extracellular enzyme that oxidatively deaminates lysine and hydroxylysine residues into reactive aldehydes (allysine), which spontaneously condense to form covalent crosslinks.
r: Correct. Lysyl oxidase requires copper to catalyze covalent collagen crosslinking.
Incorrect. Prolyl hydroxylase is intracellular and requires vitamin C and iron.
Incorrect. Lysyl hydroxylase requires vitamin C and iron.
Incorrect. Procollagen peptidase cleaves propeptides.
items.kp: Extracellular lysyl oxidase requires copper to oxidize lysine into reactive allysine aldehydes, creating covalent crosslinks that give collagen tensile strength.

items.q: A 4-year-old child presents with multiple recurrent bone fractures after minor trauma, blue sclerae, and early conductive hearing loss. Radiographs reveal diffuse osteopenia. What is the molecular defect?
o: Defect in type I collagen synthesis due to COL1A1 or COL1A2 mutations (Osteogenesis imperfecta)
Defect in type II collagen synthesis
Defect in type III collagen synthesis
items.exp: Osteogenesis imperfecta (brittle bone disease) is most commonly caused by autosomal dominant mutations in COL1A1 or COL1A2. Quantitative or qualitative defects in type I collagen produce fragile bones, blue sclerae, and hearing loss.
r: Correct. Type I collagen defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta with blue sclerae and fractures.
Incorrect. Type II collagen is in cartilage and vitreous humor.
Incorrect. Type III collagen defects cause vascular Ehlers-Danlos.
Incorrect. Fibrillin-1 defects cause Marfan syndrome.

items.q: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (vEDS) is characterized by severe fragility of arteries, bowel, and gravid uterus, predisposing to spontaneous fatal rupture. Mutations in which collagen gene are responsible?
items.exp: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is caused by heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 encoding type III collagen (reticulin), which forms the structural framework of blood vessels, gastrointestinal walls, and uterus.
r: Correct. COL3A1 mutations in type III collagen cause vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Incorrect. COL1A1 causes osteogenesis imperfecta or classic EDS.
Incorrect. COL5A1 causes classic hypermobile/hyperextensible EDS.
Incorrect. COL4A5 causes Alport syndrome.

items.q: Alport syndrome is an inherited nephropathy featuring progressive hematuria, proteinuria, sensorineural deafness, and anterior lenticonus. What type of collagen is defective in the basement membrane?
o: Type IV collagen (COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5)
items.exp: Alport syndrome is most commonly an X-linked mutation in COL4A5 encoding the alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen. Type IV collagen forms the meshwork of basement membranes in glomeruli, cochlea, and lens.
r: Correct. Type IV collagen mutations cause Alport syndrome with glomerulonephritis and deafness.
Incorrect. Type I collagen is in bone and skin.
Incorrect. Type II collagen is in cartilage.
Incorrect. Type III collagen is in reticular fibers.
items.kp: Alport syndrome results from type IV collagen alpha-chain mutations, disrupting glomerular basement membranes, cochlear function, and ocular lens shape.

items.q: Marfan syndrome is caused by autosomal dominant mutations in the FBN1 gene. What glycoprotein does FBN1 encode, and what is its extracellular matrix role?
o: Fibrillin-1, which forms microfibrils that serve as a scaffold for elastin deposition and sequesters TGF-beta
items.exp: FBN1 encodes fibrillin-1, an extracellular glycoprotein that forms microfibrils surrounding elastin. Defective fibrillin-1 impairs elastic tissue integrity and causes excessive TGF-beta signaling, predisposing to aortic root aneurysm.
r: Correct. Fibrillin-1 forms microfibrils for elastin assembly and regulates TGF-beta bioavailability.
Incorrect. Elastin is encoded by ELN.
Incorrect. Fibronectin is an integrin-binding glycoprotein.
Incorrect. Aggrecan is a proteoglycan.

items.q: Elastin is a highly resilient extracellular protein that permits reversible stretching of lungs, large arteries, and skin. What unique covalent crosslinks between lysine residues give elastin its rubber-like recoil?
o: Salt bridges between arginine and aspartate
items.exp: Lysyl oxidase deaminates three allysine residues and one unmodified lysine to condense into heterocyclic desmosine and isodesmosine rings, crosslinking four elastin polypeptides into an extensible rubber-like network.
r: Correct. Desmosine and isodesmosine crosslinks confer elasticity to elastin.
Incorrect. Elastin is low in cysteine and lacks disulfide crosslinks.
Incorrect. Hydroxyproline stabilizes collagen, not elastin recoil.
Incorrect. Salt bridges do not provide rubber-like recoil.

items.q: Classic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is characterized by velvety hyperextensible skin, fragile skin that splits with 'cigarette-paper' scarring, and generalized joint hypermobility. Mutations in which collagen type are typical?
items.exp: Classic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in COL5A1 or COL5A2 encoding type V collagen, which regulates the fibril diameter and assembly of type I collagen fibrils.
r: Correct. Type V collagen mutations cause classic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Incorrect. Type I mutations cause osteogenesis imperfecta.
Incorrect. Type III mutations cause vascular EDS.
Incorrect. Type IV mutations cause Alport syndrome.

items.q: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency leads to early panacinar pulmonary emphysema and liver cirrhosis. What is the mechanism of lung destruction?
o: Unopposed destruction of alveolar elastin by neutrophil elastase
Excessive crosslinking of collagen by lysyl oxidase
Deposition of amyloid fibrils in bronchial cartilage
items.exp: Alpha-1 antitrypsin is a serpin that neutralizes neutrophil elastase in lower airways. In AAT deficiency, uninhibited elastase degrades alveolar wall elastin, destroying alveolar septa and causing panacinar emphysema.
r: Correct. Unopposed neutrophil elastase destroys alveolar elastin in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
Incorrect. Collagen crosslinking is unaffected.
Incorrect. Amyloid is not the mechanism of emphysema.
Incorrect. Ciliary dyskinesia is Kartagener syndrome.
